en: Explosive growth of CapEx, explosive growth of NVIDIA revenues, and then, quote, at some point in time, a normalization of growth, which will allow end-user demand to catch up, and therefore, the hyperscalers will become cash flow positive again, and the world will be wonderful again, and you can value things on a multiple of free cash flow.
zh: 资本支出爆炸式增长，NVIDIA 收入爆炸式增长，然后，原话是，在某个时点，增长会正常化，这将使终端用户需求赶上，因此，超大规模云厂商将重新变为现金流为正，世界将再次美好，你就可以用自由现金流的倍数来估值。

en: And of course, every time everyone decides to double down on more CapEx, that date gets pushed out, which is another way of saying the end user demand has to be bigger to make the math work.
zh: 当然，每当大家决定在更多资本支出上加倍下注，那个日期就被推后，换句话说，终端用户需求必须更大，数学才能成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: And clearly, NVIDIA got the signal from their customers, the hyperscalers, the CoreWeaves, the OpenAIs and Tropics themselves, the Googles, that basically said, we probably at one point, everyone's analyst models were, we'll spend a lot this year, but so help me God, we'll slow down next year.
zh: 显然，NVIDIA 从他们的客户那里得到了信号——超大规模云厂商、CoreWeave 们、OpenAI 们和 Tropics 们自己，还有 Google 们——基本上说，我们可能在某个时点，每个人的分析师模型都是：我们今年会花很多，但老天作证，我们明年会放缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now those same models are saying, we spent a lot this year, and we're not going to slow down next year.
zh: 而现在那些同样的模型在说：我们今年花了很多，而我们明年不会放缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all green and go now, which is different than saying it'll be green and go forever.
zh: 现在是一路绿灯放行，这不等于是说它将永远一路绿灯放行。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, 70% guidance in a world where everyone was saying, oh, in 2027, things will start to normalize.
zh: 但是，是的，在一个人人都说“哦，到 2027 年一切将开始正常化”的世界里，给出了 70% 的指引。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, this was a statement.
zh: 不，这是一个声明。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, the biggest semiconductor market in the world is going to continue to grow at 70% instead of a typical 10% for another year.
zh: 不，世界上最大的半导体市场将在接下来的一年里继续以 70% 而非典型的 10% 增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a big ass statement.
zh: 这是个相当重磅的声明。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sound you hear is the Google free cash flow and the Oracle free cash flow just disappearing down the drain, man.
zh: 你听到的那个声音，是 Google 的自由现金流和 Oracle 的自由现金流正消失在下水道里，老兄。

speaker: Unknown
en: They better be right.
zh: 他们最好是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thanks for the intro quote there, Rory.
zh: 好了，感谢你那个开场引语，Rory。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second part of my statement was, and it was further reiterated about their buying Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.
zh: 我那句话的第二部分是——而且这一点被进一步重申了——关于他们以 129 亿美元收购 Hugging Face。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still, I don't think it's finalized or confirmed by any means, but it's definitely much more advanced than when we last discussed it.
zh: 还没有，我认为无论如何都还没最终敲定或确认，但它肯定比我们上次讨论时进展了好多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything subsequent to our last discussion that we should add or think about?
zh: 在我们上次讨论之后，有什么需要补充或思考的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Man making $120 billion a year selling compute decides to buy a company that help makes compute more cost-effective so he can sell more compute.
zh: 一个每年靠卖算力赚 1200 亿美元的人，决定收购一家能帮着让算力更具成本效益的公司，这样他就能卖出更多算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the summary of the deal.
zh: 这笔交易概括起来就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the margin, if you're NVIDIA, you were ecstatic that OpenAI and Anthropic happened because they proved that the market you were in was bigger than anyone ever imagined.
zh: 从边际上讲，如果你是 NVIDIA,你会为 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的出现而欣喜若狂，因为它们证明了你所处的市场比任何人曾经想象的都要大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And early on, no one could have done what OpenAI did.
zh: 而在早期，没有人能做成 OpenAI 做成的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, NVIDIA has been a real beneficiary of that.
zh: 因此，NVIDIA 一直是这件事的真正受益者。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now that the category is established, the simple question is,
zh: 但如今这个品类已经确立，简单的问题就是，

speaker: Unknown
en: If end users have a trillion dollars to spend on tokens, as NVIDIA, you'd prefer that money flow to open source people at 30% gross margins, where you can get all that compute, versus 70% gross margins at OpenAI or Anthropic, where they keep more of the money.
zh: 如果终端用户有 1 万亿美元要花在 token 上，作为 NVIDIA,你会更希望这些钱流向毛利率 30% 的开源阵营，这样你能拿下所有那些算力生意，而不是流向毛利率 70% 的 OpenAI 或 Anthropic,它们会把更多的钱留在自己手里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Open source is good for compute salespeople.
zh: 开源对卖算力的人有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're selling GPUs, you want everyone else's margin to be lower, so yours can be higher.
zh: 如果你在卖 GPU,你会希望其他所有人的利润率都更低，这样你的才能更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's just exactly right and rational.
zh: 所以这完全正确，完全理性。

en: I do think it's more than that.
zh: 我确实认为不止如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're right, of course, Rory.
zh: 当然，我觉得你是对的，Rory。

en: I think it's more that just NVIDIA is playing an endgame now where it has to win every segment of the market.
zh: 我觉得更多的是，NVIDIA 现在在打一场终局之战，它必须赢得市场的每一个细分领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just has to win open weights.
zh: 它就是必须赢得 open weights。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that means overpaying for Hugging Face at $110 million in ARR, if that means subsidizing whoever, it doesn't matter.
zh: 如果这意味着为 Hugging Face 支付 1.1 亿美元 ARR 对应的过高价格，如果这意味着补贴随便谁，都无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that it...
zh: 这倒不是说它……

en: I don't know that NVIDIA wants OpenWeights to beat Grok and OpenAI.
zh: 我不确定 NVIDIA 是不是想让 OpenWeights 打败 Grok 和 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just needs to, it's just clear, and that was why that memo from a couple weeks back, or memos that Jensen did his first tweet ever, right, in support of OpenWeights.
zh: 它只是需要，事情很清楚，这就是为什么几周前那份备忘录，或者说那些备忘录，黄仁勋发了他的史上第一条推文，对吧，来支持 OpenWeights。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just have to win, he's just committed to winning everything.
zh: 他们就是必须赢，他就是铁了心要赢得一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever LLM, whatever inference is, he's committed to winning a majority stake, 70%, 80% of every dollar here.
zh: 无论 LLM 是什么，无论推理是什么，他都铁了心要拿下多数份额，这里每一美元的 70%、80%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so 12.9 is, you know, no way I think it's worth it in isolation, but if it helps reinforce that, it's utterly defensible.
zh: 所以 12.9 嘛，你知道，孤立地看我绝不认为它值这个价，但如果它有助于强化那件事，那它完全站得住脚。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's utterly deficient, but it's a moment in time.
zh: 它完全有缺陷，但这是特定时刻的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would sell too.
zh: 我也会卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would sell.
zh: 我会卖。

en: Clem, good job.
zh: Clem,干得好。

en: I would sell too.
zh: 我也会卖。

en: What, did Hugging Face start off as social network for people like pets or something like that?
zh: 什么，Hugging Face 一开始是个给养宠物的人之类的社交网络还是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a Tamagotchi for like teenage loneliness.
zh: 它就是一个为了青少年孤独感而做的 Tamagotchi。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, this is the greatest tilt of the history of mankind.
zh: 是啊，我是说，这是人类历史上最伟大的一次转向。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这比 Cursor 从某个 CAD 工具之类的转型要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the tilt hero.
zh: 这是转向界的英雄。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it is interesting in terms of the sign of the times.
zh: 你知道，就时代的标志而言，这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Slack was bought for $27 billion, which is rough and tough twice what Hugging Face apparently is going to get bought of.
zh: 你知道，Slack 当年以 270 亿美元被收购，大约是 Hugging Face 显然将获得的收购价的两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we fell out of our chairs and it was the high watermark of that era, right?
zh: 当时我们都惊得从椅子上跌下来，而那是那个时代的高水位线，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was.
zh: 确实是。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it wasn't a billion in ARR.
zh: 但它当时并没有 10 亿美元 ARR。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess it makes sense.
zh: 所以我想这也说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best premium should be an order of magnitude higher than the high watermark of the last era, but it's still loopy.
zh: 最好的收购溢价应该比上一个时代的高水位线高一个数量级，但这仍然很离谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

zh: 为什么这两个孩子就不能好好相处呢，伙计们？

zh: 我们多么热爱和你合作啊，Sam。

zh: 我觉得他的回应非常精彩。

zh: 优雅，但同时又是一记贬损。

zh: 嗯，首先，这不是万能药，但你可以在 Cursor 里自带密钥。

en: So some of it is theatrics here.
zh: 所以这里面有些是做戏。

zh: 那个 5% 的说法我还在消化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我是说，这个人很记仇。

en: Anthropic, Grok, Twitter, these are like great grudge companies.

zh: 我还认为 Anthropic 重申了他们很乐意继续供货。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you zoom out, why did it happen?
zh: 而且如果你拉远看，这事为什么会发生？

zh: 最初，创始投资人之一，可以说就是那位创始投资人，是 Elon。

zh: 就算是你和我，Jason,就算我们是那两家公司之一，我们也会打起来。

en: Now, take that and then add two people who loathe each other.
zh: 现在，在这之上再加上两个彼此厌恶的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's made for TV.
zh: 这简直是给电视量身定做的剧本。

en: And the big argument that OpenAI has that's hard to argue with is, you know, in court in Oakland, Elon basically said that, you know, they hadn't abided by the terms of service.
zh: 而 OpenAI 那个很难反驳的大论点是，你知道，在奥克兰的法庭上，Elon 基本上说了，你知道，他们没有遵守服务条款。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, if you're OpenAI, this gets into the whole distillation thing, am I providing these people, are they going to use these models in ways I haven't intended to essentially distill my IP, allow them to get a head start on building their own model?
zh: 因此，如果你是 OpenAI,这就牵扯到整个蒸馏的问题：我是不是在给这些人提供……他们会不会用我未曾打算的方式使用这些模型，从而本质上蒸馏我的知识产权，让他们在构建自己的模型上抢占先机？

speaker: Unknown
en: And which means I'm effectively giving away my IP to a company who's going to leverage that to build a competitive product much cheaper than it was for me to do, just leveraging off what I've done.
zh: 而这意味着我实际上是在把我的知识产权白送给一家公司，他们会利用它以比我便宜得多的成本打造出一个有竞争力的产品，纯粹就是搭我所做成果的便车。

en: So it's not irrational.
zh: 所以这并非不理性。

zh: 某件事小家子气，不代表它就不对。

en: I mean, again, Anthropic did the same thing with Windsurf when we started this show, right?
zh: 我是说，再说一次，Anthropic 在我们这个节目开播时就对 Windsurf 做过同样的事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's happened before.
zh: 以前也发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen, I don't know for sure.
zh: 听着，我不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: My guess is this was the right move for OpenAI.
zh: 我猜这对 OpenAI 来说是正确的举动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you go from someone that was both a partner and a competitor, right, and keeping them honest, to someone that's now a direct competitor.
zh: 就是说，你从既是伙伴又是对手的人——对吧，还能让他们保持诚实——变成了如今一个直接的竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's only 5% anyway, Sam's losing no money.
zh: 反正如果只有 5%,Sam 没亏钱。

en: There's no revenue lost here, right?
zh: 这里没有损失任何收入，对吧？

en: So I would probably do it.
zh: 所以我很可能也会这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jason, you are, and I'm just going to go even further, because you forget these things.
zh: Jason,你是的，而且我还要更进一步说，因为你们忘了这些事情。

en: the reason they were in Oakland is because Elon sued OpenAI.
zh: 他们之所以在奥克兰，是因为 Elon 起诉了 OpenAI。

en: And the point is this.
zh: 重点是这个。

en: In life, you shouldn't do business with people who've recently sued you.

en: If I sued you, Harry, over something last week, and we took you to the mat, got you to go to court somewhere in East Essex, and took a week out of your life, kind of embarrassed you, made a pain in the ass, made you do a whole bunch of depo, and then two weeks later, I said, Harry, can I come on the show?
zh: 如果我上周因为某件事起诉了你，Harry,我们把你逼到墙角，让你去东埃塞克斯某个地方的法庭，占用你人生的一周时间，让你有点难堪，让你烦得要命，让你做一大堆庭外取证，然后两周后，我说：Harry,我能上你的节目吗？

zh: 显然 Elon 把这事搞得超私人化，你知道我在人生中肯定也犯过这种错：无论你有什么纠纷，就是别把它私人化；无论你怎么做，都没有好处，这看起来像是有好处，但它对 Sam 没起作用，你知道吗，对 Trump 也没用，就像，我就是不擅长这个，就是别把它私人化，该争执就争执，但就是别把它私人化。

en: I think it's spot on, Jason.

en: So yeah, I don't think it was petty.

en: God, it felt like a Tour de France race.

en: If they deliver the outcomes, you will shrink over time.
zh: 如果是它们交付结果，你就会随着时间推移而萎缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is why, again, to chime in, which is why Salesforce just bought Intercom where we were lucky enough to invest less than a year ago.
zh: 这就是为什么——再说一次，我插一句——这就是为什么 Salesforce 刚刚收购了 Intercom,我们不到一年前有幸投资了那家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a very outcome-based product for customer support, where they charge based on resolutions.
zh: 而且那是一个非常以结果为导向的客户支持产品，它们按解决数收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I go back to credit to Benioff.
zh: 再说一次，我要把功劳归于 Benioff。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's accepting that his system of record business has to be open to other front ends.
zh: 他在接受，他的记录系统业务必须对其他前端开放。

speaker: Unknown
en: And separately, he's saying, but if we want to play the outcome game, I'm not going to just walk away.
zh: 另外他在说，但如果我们想玩结果这场游戏，我不会就这么走开。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not going to just walk away and say, oh, you caught me.
zh: 他不会就这么走开然后说，哦，你抓到我了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm headless.
zh: 我是无头的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just going to be the back end.
zh: 我就只当后端。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's also buying things like Intercom to say, maybe we can sell those outcome-based deals too.
zh: 他也在收购像 Intercom 这样的东西，来表明，也许我们也能卖那些基于结果的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't look at Salesforce and say, it's obvious that you'd pile in a ton more because it will outperform from here the way you could have done four months ago.
zh: 我不会看着 Salesforce 说，很明显你应该再大量加仓，因为它会从这里开始跑赢，就像四个月前你可以做的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm sitting there with my holding as part of my portfolio and saying, this is not a casualty of the war.
zh: 但我拿着我的持仓作为投资组合的一部分坐在那里说，这不是这场战争的牺牲品。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a compounder, not a rocket ship, but a good compounder with decent cash flows and a decent valuation.
zh: 这是一家复利型公司，不是火箭飞船，而是一家有不错现金流和不错估值的优质复利型公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of go, yeah, plus or minus the S&P, maybe, whatever.
zh: 你会有点想说，行吧，加减个标普指数吧，也许吧，随便。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the train wreck people thought it was four or five months ago.
zh: 它不是人们四五个月前以为的那种火车失事。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you remember the hysteria four or five months ago.
zh: 如果你还记得四五个月前的那种歇斯底里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was hysteria.
zh: 那确实是歇斯底里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a, everyone will vibe code their own CRM on the 20VC podcast.
zh: 那是那种「人人都会 vibe code 自己的 CRM」,在 20VC 播客上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It became a hysteria, right?
zh: 它变成了一种歇斯底里，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think some people will at some people's stages, but they won't do it for the kind of customer service.
zh: 我的意思是，我认为有些人会在某些阶段这么做，但他们不会为那种客户服务这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I just want to throw in passing another number that I keep an eye on.
zh: 然后我想顺带再抛出另一个我一直在留意的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jason, and you mentioned this before, is that remember we talked about how much do you spend on models as a percentage of what you spend on engineering?
zh: Jason,你之前提到过这个，就是记得我们聊过你在模型上花的钱占你在工程上花的钱的百分比是多少吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're fully loaded.
zh: 你是按全口径算的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Salesforce spends $6 billion a year on engineering.
zh: Salesforce 每年在工程上花 60 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that probably includes QA and all the rest of it.
zh: 那可能还包括 QA 和其他所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's the right comp.
zh: 但那才是正确的对标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're going to spend $300 million this year on Anthropic.
zh: 他们今年要在 Anthropic 上花 3 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's only 5%.
zh: 所以只有 5%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when he mentioned that number a while back, you actually said the right thing, Jason, which is that still feels small.
zh: 而且他前段时间提到那个数字时，你实际上说了正确的话，Jason,那就是这感觉还是很小。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the best software company in B2B SaaS is still only spending 5% of its engineering budget on tokens, then either market is smaller than we think for intelligence, or B, people like Salesforce have a lot more to do.
zh: 如果 B2B SaaS 里最好的软件公司仍然只把 5% 的工程预算花在 token 上，那么要么智能的市场比我们想的要小，要么 B,像 Salesforce 这样的公司还有很多要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was just an interesting number.
zh: 但这只是一个有趣的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: They thought they're going to spend $300 million this year on Anthropic, which sounds like a lot in the abstract, and it is.
zh: 他们认为自己今年会在 Anthropic 上花 3 亿美元，这在抽象上听起来很多，而且确实很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you go back to the math in the upcoming Anthropic S1, if you think about your market TAM as a percentage of the engineering spend, then you probably need that probably 300 million needs to be 600 million or maybe a billion.
zh: 但如果你回到即将到来的 Anthropic S1 里的那笔数学账，如果你把你的市场 TAM 想成工程支出的一个百分比，那么你可能需要——可能那 3 亿需要变成 6 亿，或者也许 10 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe and PayPal, no more, it would seem.
zh: Stripe 和 PayPal,没戏了，看起来是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Deal is off.
zh: 交易告吹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've spoken about it a lot, saying about the amazing nature of doing it while private, the strategic bet that it was.
zh: 我们已经谈论过它很多次，说到在还私有的时候就做这件事的惊人之处，以及那是一个怎样的战略押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now it's off.
zh: 现在它告吹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's as simple as price.
zh: 我认为原因就这么简单：价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the rumor is the Stripe Advent Syndicate offered in the 60s and PayPal wanted in the 70s and, you know, stocks bounced off the low.
zh: 我认为传言是 Stripe Advent Syndicate 出价在 60 多，而 PayPal 想要 70 多，而且，你知道，股价已经从低点反弹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know it's a smart deal to try and do, but they're clearly not willing to overpay as they see it.
zh: 而且我知道试图做成这笔交易是聪明的，但按他们自己的看法，他们显然不愿意多付。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is always a dance and we never know where we are in the dance.
zh: 这始终是一场舞，而我们永远不知道自己在这支舞的哪一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: PayPal, when the deal was worked on, PayPal was at 42, right?
zh: PayPal,当交易在进行的时候，PayPal 在 42,对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: As the deal progressed, it was at 61.
zh: 随着交易的推进，它在 61。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it collapsed to 53, right?
zh: 然后它跌到了 53,对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So Stripe's still looking at this as a $41 company, right?
zh: 所以 Stripe 仍然把这看作是一家 41 美元的公司，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Advent, they've run their models.
zh: 而 Advent,他们已经跑过他们的模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And PayPal called their bluff and their stock crashed as a result.
zh: 而 PayPal 拆穿了他们的虚张声势，结果他们的股价崩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we just, it's actually an incredibly, to someone like me, it's an incredibly annoying dance.
zh: 所以我们就是，对像我这样的人来说，这实际上是一种极其烦人的舞步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't we just get to the end of the dance?
zh: 为什么我们就不能直接走到这支舞的结尾？

speaker: Unknown
en: But these deals often, not only do you have to make a second offer, but they have to fall apart after the second offer in order to ever happen.
zh: 但这些交易往往是这样：你不仅得报第二次价，而且还得让它在第二次报价之后破裂，交易才最终能成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there's a lot of structural reasons, right?
zh: 就是说有很多结构性的原因，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the board has theater and drama.
zh: 而董事会是有表演和戏码的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There may be no way to get one more dollar out of the deal than for it to fall apart.
zh: 也许只有让交易破裂，才能从交易里多挤出一块钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's not say it's dead until it's dead.
zh: 在它真的死了之前，先别说它死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm skeptical.
zh: 我持怀疑态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a good point.
zh: 我觉得这话说得有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a dance that goes on, right?
zh: 是有一套舞步在进行的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my God, this dance.
zh: 哦天哪，这种舞步。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like venture before AI where you could walk from a hot deal and then come back.
zh: 这就像 AI 之前的风投时代，你可以从一笔热门交易中走开，然后又能回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the founder wanted 1 billion pre-revenue.
zh: 你知道，创始人想要 10 亿的 pre-revenue 估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: You only wanted to do 500.
zh: 而你只肯做 5 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could walk and a couple of weeks later you could meet in the middle, but not today.
zh: 你可以走开，几周后再折中见面，但今天不行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any others that we should discuss?
zh: 还有哪些是我们应该讨论的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Polymarket raises a billion at 21 billion.
zh: Polymarket 以 210 亿估值融资 10 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I said, Linea announces $100 million ARR growing 100% doing a tender.
zh: 正如我所说，Linea 宣布 1 亿美元 ARR、增长 100%,正在做一轮要约收购(tender)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clay raising at $7 billion led by Wellington.
zh: Clay 以 70 亿估值融资，由 Wellington 领投。

speaker: Unknown
en: Texas pausing flock camera usage.
zh: 德克萨斯州暂停使用 flock 摄像头。

speaker: Unknown
en: A quick note on Clay.
zh: 关于 Clay 简单说两句。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just thought it was very interesting for us at $7 billion.
zh: 我只是觉得对我们来说，70 亿这个点非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started out as a Clay skeptic and have become a Clay convert over the years.
zh: 我一开始是个 Clay 怀疑论者，这些年变成了 Clay 的皈依者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a skeptic because when AI sucked, every CMO wanted to check the box on being an AI hero when to bring in Clay.
zh: 我当时是怀疑论者，因为在 AI 还很烂的时候，每个 CMO 都想在“当 AI 英雄”这一项上打个勾，然后把 Clay 引进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you remember that from like a year and a half ago?
zh: 你还记得大概一年半前的那种情况吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm gonna get fired.
zh: 就是，“我要被炒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I better have an AI tool.
zh: 我最好得有一个 AI 工具。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And Clay just benefited from this rush to check the box.
zh: 而 Clay 正是受益于这股抢着打勾的潮流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't see it in the product.
zh: 而我在产品里没看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the marketing annoyed me that every CMO at like Saster A annual two years ago was buying Clay.
zh: 而且那些营销让我很烦——两年前的 Saster A annual 上，每个 CMO 都在买 Clay。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, more power to the founders, but this check the box because I'm going to get fired annoyed me.
zh: 我是说，愿创始人越做越好，但这种“因为我要被炒了所以打个勾”的做法让我很烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will tell you, I've changed my mind and our agents will only use Clay now for real.
zh: 我告诉你，我已经改主意了，我们的智能体现在真的只会用 Clay。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will use nothing but Clay.
zh: 它们什么都不会用，只用 Clay。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as we move from...
zh: 所以随着我们从……

speaker: Unknown
en: AEO and GEO and whatever-EO to agent-made decisions.
zh: AEO、GEO 和随便什么-EO,走向由智能体做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact our agents would only use Clay, I think it's a BF deal.
zh: 我们的智能体只会用 Clay 这个事实，我认为这是一笔 BF 交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have moved everything that we do to Clay, not only because it's a great product, but it's not worth arguing with the agents.
zh: 所以我们已经把我们做的所有东西都搬到了 Clay 上，不仅因为它是个很棒的产品，还因为跟智能体争论不值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this is the most stubborn I've seen our agents.
zh: 这是 我见过我们的智能体最固执的一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: You anthropomorphized.
zh: 你拟人化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stubborn is a human strength.
zh: 固执是人类的一种优点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really did, but I only have so much time in the day.
zh: 我确实是拟人化了，但我一天只有这么多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the agent's going to say six times you must use clay, I will concede defeat and use clay.
zh: 如果智能体要说六遍“你必须用 clay”,我就认输，用 clay。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in a sense, I think it might be the cheapest it's ever been at $7 billion.
zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我认为 70 亿这个估值可能是它有史以来最便宜的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if we're moving to an agent-first world, then agents will insist on using products.
zh: 因为如果我们正走向一个智能体优先的世界，那么智能体会坚持使用某些产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, it may not last.
zh: 当然，这可能不会持久。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the agents will say something different in a year.
zh: 也许一年后智能体会说出不一样的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is one of the handful of products where the agents were so insistent you must use Clay that I'm all in on those, buy those, like load up those stocks.
zh: 但这是极少数产品之一——智能体如此坚持“你必须用 Clay”——所以我全押这类，买这些，就像满仓买入这些股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jason, welcome to the IC.
zh: Jason,欢迎来到 IC。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have Rory and Harry as your partners.
zh: 你的搭档是 Rory 和 Harry。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the bull case from this point?
zh: 从这一点来看,看涨的理由是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: This may be the cheapest round at 7 billion.
zh: 这可能是 70 亿估值下最便宜的一轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fantastic.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the bull case for where this goes and how big is that?
zh: 这家公司会走向何方的看涨理由是什么?那个市场有多大?

speaker: Unknown
en: The bull case is that agentic GDM has just started, right?
zh: 看涨的理由是,智能体化的 GDM 才刚刚开始,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And much like the three of us made a mistake not going early into cognition,
zh: 就像我们三个犯了个错误,没有早点进入 Cognition,

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we thought the TAM was too small.
zh: 因为我们当时觉得 TAM 太小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also thought the TAM was too small for a Gentic GTM.
zh: 我们也认为 Gentic GTM 的 TAM 太小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought the TAM was the same as it was.
zh: 我们以为 TAM 和原来的一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out when agents can run these GTM motions, they will consume 10 to 100 times more usage than humans ever could.
zh: 结果发现,当智能体可以执行这些 GTM 动作时,它们的消耗量会是人类可能达到的 10 到 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can run GTM around the clock.
zh: 它们可以全天候运行 GTM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not talking about spamming.
zh: 我说的不是垃圾群发。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm talking about analyzed, consistent campaigns, reaching every prospect, reaching every customer across the globe.
zh: 我说的是经过分析、持续一致的活动,触达每一个潜在客户,触达全球每一个客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Clay's the clear leader there.
zh: 而 Clay 在这方面是明显的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need exposure, but it is the clear leader.
zh: 我们需要敞口,但它确实是明显的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents will consume 20x more GTM resources, more tokens, more usage.
zh: 智能体将消耗 20 倍的 GTM 资源、更多的 token、更多的使用量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if revenue doesn't go up all that much, not everyone that's coding is really seeing a revenue lift from it.
zh: 即使收入没有涨那么多,并不是每个写代码的人都真正从中看到了收入提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone using all this agentic GTM will radically close qualified pipeline, but the usage is just going to explode and Clay is a clear breakout winner and it's accelerating.
zh: 不是每个使用这些智能体 GTM 的人都会激进地关单合格的 pipeline,但使用量会爆炸式增长,Clay 是明显的突围赢家,而且还在加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I can see a path to a hundred billion and I recommend a small initial $150 million stake.
zh: 所以我能看到一条通往一千亿的路,我建议初始投入一笔 1.5 亿美元的小额持仓。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Andreessen Growth Fund is ringing to hire you as we speak, Jason.
zh: 我们说话这会儿,Andreessen 成长基金正在打电话来雇你呢,Jason。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll be great.
zh: 你会很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're underestimating this trend, both of them, how much agents are going to do things in GTM, just like voting.
zh: 我认为我们低估了这个趋势,两个趋势,低估了智能体在 GTM 中会做多少事情,就像投票一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But man, this agent, Rory's right, don't anthropomorphize them.
zh: 但是天哪,这个智能体,Rory 说得对,不要把它们拟人化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But sometimes when it's just you, you got to.
zh: 但有时候当你只有自己一个人时,你不得不这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, you can't get past the task.
zh: 否则,你无法完成这个任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think they and Lenny are versions of a story that says, if you grab hold of these changes as a founder, you can turn change into your advantage, even if you're an older company.
zh: 我认为他们和 Lenny 都是同一个故事的不同版本,这个故事说的是,作为创始人,如果你抓住这些变化,你就能把变化变成你的优势,即使你是一家老公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, Clay, you're right.
zh: 因为,Clay,你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: The initial product wasn't an AI product.
zh: 最初的产品不是 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a waterfalling product for various different data sources like Zoom and all the other kind of Zoom sources.
zh: 它是一个面向各种不同数据源的瀑布式产品,比如 Zoom 和所有其他那种 Zoom 源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a very good, very point product for RevOps.
zh: 对 RevOps 来说,它是一个非常好的、非常单点的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they've done an excellent job of riding the marketing hype around go-to-market AI.
zh: 而且他们非常出色地乘上了围绕 go-to-market AI 的营销炒作东风。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on top of that, actually generating real product in that space.
zh: 然后在此基础上,真正在那个领域做出了实打实的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also mentioned Linear, which is doing really nicely, doubling at 100%.
zh: 我们还提到了 Linear,它做得非常好,以 100% 的速度翻倍增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: My point is these are companies that were founded pre-gen AI that have done a really nice job at the app level of co-attaching to the AI trends and are looking at their survivors.
zh: 我的意思是,这些公司成立于生成式 AI 之前,在应用层面非常出色地共同附着到了 AI 趋势上,并且正在看着他们的幸存者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more than that.
zh: 我认为不止如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to be clear why, and I can talk about Linear briefly if we're not running out of time.
zh: 让我说清楚为什么,如果我们时间还没耗尽的话,我可以简短谈谈 Linear。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think they just attach to trends.
zh: 我不认为它们只是附着在趋势上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is a really important phrase.
zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are incredibly agent friendly.
zh: 它们对智能体极其友好。
